newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch closing share market report.
newsitem.headline: Dutch closing share market report.

text.p: Dutch shares closed higher on Tuesday, squeezing up in relatively low volume after a couple of directionless sessions on the feeling that the Federal Reserve is unlikely to raise U.S. interest rates this week.
The Fed's two-day Open Market Committee meeting is due to start later on Tuesday and analysts believe U.S. inflation is tame enough for the Fed to keep monetary policy unchanged.

The AEX closed 5.45 points higher at 680.22, after bumping against near term resistance of 682. "The market is up today because people are betting that the Fed won't do anything on interest rates for the moment," said one dealer.
Dealers said the market could be set to break out above its January 23 all-time high of 686.01 later this week if the Fed leaves interest rates unchanged.
"People still want to invest in this market, there's a lot of money that can come in from the pension funds and if rates stay unchanged we can go through the old high," a dealer said.

"We've been in a stabilisation phase for the last week or so where we've moved up five points and then moved down that much, this is still part of that process," said another dealer. He also believed the next positive economic development could be enough to push the AEX higher, possibly towards 700 this month.

"The U.S. is very important right now," said the dealer. "If we've got to deal with a small (U.S.) rate increase then we've got a problem, but if it doesn't happen then I think the market looks quite positive and could be ready for another upturn."

KLM closed 60 cents lower at 53.90 guilders, falling after it reported a third quarter net loss of 7.0 million guilders, down from a 102 million profit a year earlier, which was broadly in line with a wide range of analysts' forecasts.
Forecasts had ranged from a loss of 54 million guilders to a profit of 12 million guilders and some analysts feared the net loss could carry on into the fourth quarter.
Food group CSM closed 4.60 guilders higher at 107.90, boosted by its forecast of a further rise in 1996/97 profit and prediction that turnover in the year would rise 20 percecent.

Nutricia closed 3.80 guilders higher at 266.30 after the company said no contaminants had been found in its Milumil baby milk powder, recently withdrawn from sale after a salmonella scare. Separately Britain's department of health said tests had shown an "association" between salmonella anatum and Milumil.

Aegon closed 90 cents higher at 113.50 guilders. It declined to comment on a report that it was one of the front-runners to buy UK life insurance mutual Scottish Amicable. -- Keiron Henderson, Amsterdam Newsroom +31 20 504 5000
